title: Entry Into Practice
markdown:
## APPENDIX

## Entry into Practice

## CONTENT OVERVIEW

- All about certification exams
- Becoming certified and licensed
- Scope of practice
- Credentialing
- Interviewing and negotiation
- Malpractice
- Credentialing (hospital & insurance)

## NOTES

## CONTENT OBJECTIVES

At the conclusion of this activity, the participant will be able to:

1. Describe the transition from RN to NP practice.
2. Plan for certification, licensure, and prescribing.
3. Recognize scope-of-practice regulation.
4. List items to include in a professional portfolio for licensure, credentialing, and recertification.
5. Identify key factors in employment negotiations and practice.

## PREPARING FOR THE CERTIFICATION EXAM

6 months from graduation

## National Certification

- Purpose
- $ To assess entry-level knowledge & competence to provide safe, quality care
- $ Assures consumers that you have met current standards of practice
- $ Meet the needs of employers, insurers, and the public
- $ Assures your commitment to lifelong learning
- $ Nearly all states require national certification for licensure and prescriptive authority

## Study Plan

- Begin studying at least 6 months in advance.
- $ Review your course materials.
- $ Study in a group format.
- $ Take an online or live review course.
- $ Take a predictor exam.
- Determine which certification exam.

## Choosing Certification

| AANP   | ANCC   | AACN         | PNCB    | NCC     |
|--------|--------|--------------|---------|---------|
| FNP    | FNP    | ACNPC-AG     | CPNP-AC | NNP-BC  |
| AGNP   | AGPCNP | ACNPC- Adult | CPNP-PC | WHNP-BC |
| PMHNP  | AGACNP |              | PMHS    |         |
| ENP    | PMHNP  |              |         |         |
|        | ENP    |              |         |         |

## Application for Certification

- Complete application 2-3 months before you plan to take the exam.
- $ Official transcript from your university
- $ Validation of education form (faculty-signed)
- Completion of the 3Ps
- Required clinical hours
- Practice sites
- $ Current RN licensure
- Notification of state licensing board
- $ Complete the document checklist!!
- Testing before graduation

## Application Tips

- Create an online profile.
- Name on application must match two forms of identification at testing center.
- Method of notification (e.g., email address)
- Keep a copy of your application.
- $ Varies: 1-6 weeks to receive authorization to test

## ANCC vs. AANP

|                                | ANCC                                                             | AANP                                       |
|--------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
| Authorization to test          | 120 days                                                         | 120 days                                   |
| Board certification credential | FNP-BC, AGPCNP-BC, AGACNP-BC, PMHNP-BC                           | FNP-C, AGNP-C                              |
| Costs-nonmember                | $395 ($295/member)                                               | $315 ($240/member)                         |
| Questions                      | 175: 150 scored, 25 pretest                                      | 150: 135 scored, 15 pretest                |
| Format                         | Multiple choice, drop and drag, hot spot, and multiple responses | Multiple choice                            |
| Time to complete               | 3.5 h                                                            | 3 h                                        |
| Results                        | Immediate; official letter in about 1 week                       | Immediate; official letter in about 1 week |

| Board certification credentials | ACNPC-AG                                   | CPNP, CPNP-AC                                      | WHNP-BC, NNP-BC                                                   |

| Questions                       | 175: 150 scored, 25 pretest                | 175: 150 scored, 25 pretest                        | 175: 150 scored, 25 pretest                                       |

| Time to complete                | 3.5 h                                      | 3 h                                                | 3 h                                                               |
| Results                         | Immediate; official letter in about 1 week | Immediate; official letter in 2-3 weeks            | Mailed within 15 days; P/F viewed in account after results mailed |

## Maintaining National Certification

|                                                | ANCC                                                                                           | AANP                                                                       |
|------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Renews                                         | 5 years                                                                                        | 5 years                                                                    |
| Cost                                           | $375 ($275/member)                                                                             | $195 ($120/member)                                                         |
| Practice hours                                 | 1,000 (optional category)                                                                      | 1,000 hours in population focus (DPC, administrative, education, research) |
| Continuing education (from approved providers) | 75                                                                                             | 100                                                                        |
| Pharmacology hours                             | 25                                                                                             | 25                                                                         |
| Other renewal categories                       | Plus 1 of the 8 renewal categories: academic credits, presentations, EBP, preceptor hours etc. | 25 CEs (nonpharm) can be substituted if precepting                         |
| Alternative                                    | Recertify by examination                                                                       | Recertify by examination                                                   |

## Maintaining National Certification

|                                             | AACN                                        | PNCB                                        | NCC                                                                                                                   |
|---------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Renews                                      | 5 years                                     | Yearly; 7-year cycle                        | 3 years                                                                                                               |
| Cost                                        | $340 option 1/$305 options 2 & 3            | Variable                                    | $100-$175                                                                                                             |
| Practice hours                              | 1,000 verifiable practice hours             | Practice hours: 400 = CH                    | Continuing competency assessment (starts the assessment cycle, IEP)                                                   |
| Contact hours (CH)                          | 150 total 75 in Cat 1 (acute care)          | 15 CH = PPL, practice, academic credit      | 10-50 hours: core competency                                                                                          |
| Pharmacology                                | 25                                          | 15                                          |                                                                                                                       |
| Other renewal categories                    | Examination                                 | Modules: 4 in 7 years                       | Precepting; presenting CE activities; authorship book/journal articles; NCC activities; item writing; academic credit |
| Alternatives are available for AACN and NCC | Alternatives are available for AACN and NCC | Alternatives are available for AACN and NCC | Alternatives are available for AACN and NCC                                                                           |

## Expired Certification

- Cease and desist!
- $ Using the title
- $ Practicing
- You must notify your BON.
- $ Threatens your licensure
- $ Threatens reimbursement

## Still Deciding?

- Certification exam
- $ Test blueprint
- $ Reference lists
- $ Certification/recertification handbook
- $ Sample questions
- $ Test tips

## Expired Certification

ANCC:

- <2 years: reactivate by renewal requirements
- ≥2 years: Complete 75 CE, retest, and pass certification exam (if not retired exam).

AANP: Complete renewal requirements.

Best practice: Renew 6 months before expiration.

## Maintaining Certification

- Current active/unencumbered license
- Online recertification dashboards
- Keep supporting documents (e.g., CE certificates).

## Schedule/Reschedule

www.prometric.com

Schedule:

- Designated testing center or live remote proctoring
- You are responsible for scheduling!
- Special accommodations

## HOW DO YOU RESCHEDULE?

- Through Prometric
- Request to cancel/reschedule (with no fee).
- $ 31 days prior to scheduled test
- $ Must be rescheduled within authorization to test window
- Request to cancel/reschedule 30 days to 24 hours (fee required).
- $ No exams can be canceled/rescheduled within 24 hours of exam appointment.
- Extensions granted for hardship (to extend 120 test window)
- Renewal/recertification handbooks
- Random audits
- Notify BON of recertification.

NOTES

## NOTES

## BECOMING CERTIFIED AND LICENSED

## Testing Center

Location nearest to you: research location

- Arrive 30 min before scheduled testing time.
- Two forms of identification (one photo)
- $ Name must match application
- $ Temporary or expired IDs are NOT acceptable
- $ Must contain signature
- $ Bring eligibility letter or ATT
- If late, missed scheduled appointment time, or arrive without proper ID:
- $ Will not be able to take their examination as scheduled.
- $ Will be responsible for paying any applicable testing center fees.
- $ Will forfeit their fee and require a new registration number.

## Testing Center: Test Day!

- Scratch paper provided; dry erase board
- Locker to store personal items
- No scheduled breaks
- No misconduct

## Did I Pass?

- Immediate results
- Detailed score report mailed (AANP/ANCC); emailed
- Certificate 3-4 weeks
- How are exams scored?
- $ Criterion-referenced examinations
- $ Scaled scoring systems
- $ Total number of correct answers, converted into consistent and standardized scale
- $ Provides direct and fair comparisons

## Retesting

- Must apply to retest
- Waiting period
- Limited number of times to retest
- $ ANCC three times in 12 months (certified within 5 years)
- $ AANP two times in a calendar year
- Eligibility to retest/retest fee

Specific criteria:

- $ Continuing education
- $ Wait until next testing window
- $ Certifying body/state limitations

## NP Licensure

- State laws individualized
- Review the requirements
- $ Active RN licensure (compact licensure)
- $ Associated fees
- $ Required documents (e.g., clinical courses/hours completed)

## Application for Licensure

## Follow the process!

- Submit application for licensure
- a. Detailed instructions on BON website
- b. Application packet
- c. Follow the checklist of required documents
- d. Official documentation
- a) Verification of graduate degree
- b) Verification of certification

## When Are You "Official"?

- Receive a specific NP license number
- Valid when license number appears on the BON website

## Postnominal Initials

- Highest earned degree (PhD, DNP, DNS)
- $ Non-nursing degrees (e.g., MEd)
- Licensure (APRN)
- Area of preparation (FNP, AGNP, PNP)
- National certification (C, BC)
- Awards and honors (FAANP)
- Other certifications (including non-nursing)

Kathy Baldridge, DNP, APRN, FNP-BC, FAANP

## SCOPE OF PRACTICE

## NOTES Know Your Scope!

<!-- image -->

## Collaborative Practice Agreements

- Dependent on your state's requirements
- Check state regulations (e.g., standard form, requirements for renewal, filed with state, kept on site)
- Not the same as an employment agreement

## Prescriptive Authority (PA)

- All 50 states and the District of Columbia
- Graduate-level pharmacology course required
- Physician involvement in PA varies by states
- $ No physician involvement
- $ Collaborative relationship
- Refer to your state BON for specific requirements
- $ Off-label prescribing
- $ Restrictions on prescribing
- Authorized to prescribe with a prescribing number

## Federal Regulations

- Centers for Medicaid and Medicare Services
- Billable practices (e.g., diabetic shoes, home health services)
- National Council of State Boards of Nursing
- E-prescribing and electronic health records
- Drug Enforcement Administration

## Portfolio

- Verification of RN licensure
- Transcript
- Course description/number, credit hours, and year taken
- Detailed syllabi to confirm didactic content, clinical labs, and procedures
- Clinical hours log
- Abstract from capstone project or thesis
- Copy of articles, projects
- Curriculum vitae

## CREDENTIALING

## National Provider ID (NPI) Number

- First number you apply for!
- National Plan & Provider Enumeration System (NPPES)
- Unique and individual identifying provider number
- $ Payers (insurance companies), pharmacies, credentialing organizations, and other interested parties

## NPI Number

- Mandated by The Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996
- https://nppes.cms.hhs.gov/#/
- $ Social security number
- $ Date of birth
- $ State nursing license
- $ Practice address(es), phone numbers, fax number
- All information is available to the public!

## NOTES

## NOTES Controlled Dangerous Substances (CDSs)

- State-specific license
- Obtain from the Board of Pharmacy
- $ May require BON authority to prescribe CDSs
- $ Must obtain prior to applying for DEA license
- $ One CDS license for each site
- $ Fee required
- $ Yearly renewal

## DEA Number

- Regulated by the Drug Enforcement Administration (under the Department of Justice [DOJ])
- $ Must have state licensure
- $ May require controlled dangerous substance (CDS) license (state level)
- DEA does not supersede CDS.
- Must be included on Rx for controlled substances
- Electronic renewal reminders
- $888/3 years renewal fee (free for federal employees)

https://www.dea.gov/

## DEA Requirements

Requires an 8-hour course of opioid training https://www.deadiversion.usdoj.gov/online\_forms\_apps.html

<!-- image -->

## Prescription Drug Monitoring Program (PDMP)

- To help detect overprescribing, diversion, and fraud
- All states and provinces have a PDMP

<!-- image -->

https://www.cdc.gov/overdose-prevention/php/interventions/prescription-drug-monitoringprograms.html?CDC\_AAref\_Val=https://www.cdc.gov/drugoverdose/pdmp/index.html

## INTERVIEWING & NEGOTIATING CONTRACT

## Why is a good CV important?

"You never get a second chance to make a good first impression!" Will Rogers

## Professional CV

- Heading: personal information/goals/profile
- Education
- Professional experience
- Preceptor locations
- Presentations
- Thesis

## Curriculum Vitae

- Keep it updated
- $ Credentialing
- $ Licenses (with expiration dates)
- $ Education and work experience are important
- $ Specialty training
- $ Professional organizations/societies
- Include in portfolio
- Community service
- Committee activity
- Honors and awards
- Research activities/grants/awards
- Quality improvement activities

NOTES

## NOTES Employment

- Is job description in alignment with scope?
- Interview skills/dress
- Do your research about the practice location! $ Employer's experience with NPs?

## Employment Contract

- Length of contract (renegotiation)
- $ 6 months, 1 year, 2 years, 3 years
- Compensation
- $ Salary/hourly
- $ Bonuses?
- $ Hours, holidays, sick leave, vacation

## Contract Terms

- Noncompete clause
- $ How long?
- $ Radius?

## Contract Negotiation

## Be strategic! Know your worth.

- New/established patients per day?
- Average E/M code per patient?
- Average reimbursement amount?
- Fair market value (community standards)
- Varies by:
- $ Practice area
- $ Education/role
- $ Geography
- Employment contract (not a CPA)
- $ Details of the position
- $ Specifics about benefits
- $ Details of the employment arrangement
- $ Expectations
- $ Agreeable by both parties
- Termination
- $ Breach of contract by either party
- $ Performance by NP
- $ Length of notice
- Performance evaluation
- $ Peer review
- $ Chart reviews
- $ Patient load
- On-call responsibilities
- Support staff (e.g., secretarial, MA)

## Projection of revenue

- Patients per day × reimbursement amount
- Estimate
- $ Initial
- $ 6 months
- $ 1 year

<!-- image -->

## Points of Negotiation

- Continuing education
- Professional memberships
- Licensure fees
- Prescriptive fees
- Communication (e.g., phone service)
- Insurance (e.g., malpractice)
- Professional needs (e.g., books, lab coats)
- Promotion of practice/NP

## Methods of Payment

- Straight salary: fixed amount to perform according to the job description
- Percentage of net receipts: payment based on the amount the NP bills, minus accounts receivable, minus the NP's portion of practice expenses (which may include expense of physician consultation)
- Base salary plus percentage: base salary guaranteed; additional salary may be earned if income over set amount is generated
- Hourly rate: payment made only for hours worked

## Typical Policy Coverage

- $1 million each claim
- Amount of a professional liability claim
- You are legally obligated to pay
- A covered medical incident
- $3 million annual aggregate, for all covered claims during the policy period

## Two Main Types of Policies

<!-- image -->

NOTES

## NOTES Malpractice

- Owned or paid for by NP? Employer?
- What does it pay for?
- $ Your defense attorney
- $ Lost wage reimbursement
- $ Court costs
- $ Licensing issues/board representation

## Things to Consider

- Employer-provided liability coverage:
- $ Policy limits may not be high enough.
- $ You may not be provided with coverage for lost wage reimbursement, licensing board hearing reimbursement, and defense costs.
- $ You may not be covered outside the workplace, such as when you engage in volunteer or part-time work.
- $ You may not be covered for lawsuits filed after you have ended your employment.

## National Nurse Practitioner Data Bank (NPDB)

- Established by Congress in 1986
- Adverse actions/malpractice
- What if I disagree with my report?
- Verify & update your address
- Submit a statement
- Dispute a report

<!-- image -->

https://www.npdb.hrsa.gov/pract/practGuide.jsp

- Cost based on:
- $ Professional role
- $ Practice setting
- $ State

## CREDENTIALING (INSURANCE & HOSPITAL)

## Credentialing Hospital & Insurance

- State license number
- Educational background
- Authorization to prescribe
- Employment background:
- $ Employment gaps explained
- NPI number
- CDC/DEA
- 3-6 month process

## Credentialing Documents

- Procedure logs, certificate of training
- Practice information: phone and fax numbers, address, contact person
- Standard care agreement
- Continuing education hour log
- Background check & fingerprinting
- National Practitioner Data Bank inquiry

## Medicare

- Provider enrollment
- https://www.cms.gov
- Internet-based enrollment
- Provider Enrollment, Chain, and Ownership System (PECOS)
- 45-60 days for approval
- NPI number and password required

## Medicaid

- Shared funding by federal & state governments
- States decide (in addition to minimal mandatory requirements)
- $ Covered populations (e.g., people without disabilities, not classified as older adults, not pregnant)
- $ Covered services (e.g., dental services, vision services)
- $ Health care delivery models (e.g., fee for service, managed care plans)
- $ Methods for paying providers
- $ Methods for paying hospitals
- Credentialing through "provider relations" in state departments of health

## NOTES

## NOTES COUNCIL FOR AFFORDABLE QUALITY HEALTHCARE (CAQH)

- Universal provider data source
- Created to simplify the credentialing process
- Free to providers
- caqh.org/providers
- Once you are credentialed with the first insurance company, a provider number is issued, and you can register online
- Attestation process every 120 days

## CAQH: Portfolio Documents

- Copies of diplomas
- Employment chronology
- References: three professional
- Practice details (e.g., address, phone number, etc.)
- National Provider Identifier number
- Malpractice:
- $ Copy of malpractice face sheet
- $ Malpractice information: address and phone number
- Workers' compensation number
- Professional licensures
- W-9
- Basic life support/advanced life support: dates

## Reimbursement/Billing

Portfolio

- Log of all billing numbers from third-party payers
- Hospital credentialing applications
- Procedural logs

<!-- image -->

## Billing and coding

- Practice within scope
- Avoid fraudulent billing
- Productivity = Revenue
- Incident-to-billing
- Split/shared billing
- Bundled/unbundled billing

## Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) Codes

- Copyrighted by AMA
- Used to describe evaluations, tests, surgeries, and medical procedures
- Know the difference between:
- $ Evaluation & Management (E/M) Codes: outpatient, inpatient, nursing home, and a variety of other settings
- $ International Classification of Diseases (ICD) 10th revision (ICD-10): unique alphanumeric codes to catalog specific diagnosis, symptoms, and procedures

Projected implementation of ICD-11 2025-2027

## APRN Responsibility to Stay Current

- National Council of State Boards of Nursing (state practice acts listed here): https://www.ncsbn. org/
- American Association of Nurse Practitioners State Practice Center: https://www.aanp.org/ legislation-regulation/state-legislation/state-practice-environment
- Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (legislative information on reimbursement and HIPAA concerns): https://www.cms.gov/

## Professional Memberships

- National and state NP organizations
- $ Continuing education opportunities
- $ Networking
- $ Level of prestige/professionalism
- $ Leadership opportunities
- $ Public & health policies
- $ Precepting
- $ Contribute to political action committees (PAC)

## Reference Links

- Apply for NPI number
- $ https://nppes.cms.hhs.gov/#/
- Enroll in CAQH
- $ https://caqh.org/provider
- Apply for DEA
- $ https://www.deadiversion.usdoj.gov/online\_forms\_apps.html
- Medicare enrollment
- $ https://www.cms.gov

## Certifying Bodies

- American Academy of Nurse Practitioners Certification Board https://www.aanpcert.org/
- American Nurses Credentialing Center https://www.nursingworld.org/our-certifications/
- American Association of Critical Care Nurses https://www.aacn.org/certification/advanced-practice
- Pediatric Nursing Certification Board https://www.pncb.org/certifications
